{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** Legal (Counsel to Customer)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. On balance, the risk-allocation architecture is strong for us: the core protections — indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law (§ 28) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) — are all compliant, and several exceed our preferred positions (notably the uncapped Excluded Claims in § 21.3 and the perpetual, fully paid licence in § 13.2).

The problems are concentrated in a small number of Vendor-favourable clauses that were bolted onto an otherwise balanced document, and three of them sit at our walk-away thresholds:

- **Exclusivity / non-compete (§ 2.2)** — an unlimited sole-supplier commitment binding us for the full term, which also contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. This single clause drives three separate findings (exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment).
- **Liquidated damages (§ 7.6)** — uncapped USD 25,000 per day payable by *us* for delay in an undefined "dependency".
- **Audit rights (§ 22.1)** — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems, which also conflicts internally with § 22.2.

We also flag a Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2), a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-hire (§ 12.4), a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2), the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right (§ 9), and a narrow warranty gap for perpetually licensed software (§ 19.2). Redlines have been prepared for each deviation; fallbacks are offered in the margin comments where sensible.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification | Meets and exceeds preferred position; Vendor indemnity sits outside the cap via § 21.3. No redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables | Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables; embedded Vendor Technology routed to the § 13.2 perpetual licence. No redline. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21 Limitation of Liability | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; all required carve-outs present. No redline. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control | Customer affiliate/successor right; Vendor consent-gated; no Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control. No redline. |
| 5 | High | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22 Audit Rights | § 22.1 permits unlimited, unannounced audits and remote system access (walk-away); conflicts with § 22.2. Redlined to one audit per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site, independent auditor, no system access. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.2 sole-supplier commitment for hosted analytics for the whole term, no scope, time or performance exit (walk-away); contradicts § 2.1. Deleted. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.6 uncapped USD 25,000/day payable by Customer for delay in an undefined "dependency" (walk-away). Deleted; fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. |
| 8 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence | Affiliates and contractors in scope; perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence; revocation only on uncured material breach. No redline. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.2 undefined field-of-use restriction with no internal-development or acquisition carve-out; contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3. Deleted; fallback offered in comment. |
| 10 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 Termination | No convenience right for either Party against a three-year term (§ 8.1) with 180 days' non-renewal notice (§ 8.2). New § 9.4 inserted: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, no Vendor convenience right. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution | New York law; exclusive jurisdiction in New York County; no arbitration provision. No redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes | § 7.2 requires Customer to extend Vendor our best terms given to any other technology supplier, unqualified as to product, duration and comparability (walk-away). Deleted. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope | § 2.2 operates as a de facto volume commitment with no reduction or exit right, contradicting §§ 2.1, 7.1 and 12.3. Deleted. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12 Customer Responsibilities | § 12.4 is one-way, 18 months, covers any Vendor employee during the term, bars "engage" as well as "solicit", no carve-outs; conflicts with § 12.3. Deleted; mutual 12-month fallback offered. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8 Term and Renewal | 12-month renewal and CPI/3% uplift cap (§ 8.3) are compliant, but the 180-day non-renewal window exceeds our 90-day walk-away threshold. Shortened to 30 days plus a Vendor 60-day renewal reminder; 60 days available as fallback. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return | Six months' assistance at expiring rates; 30-day machine-readable return; no withholding for fee disputes. No redline. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance | CGL, E&O, USD 5M cyber, workers' compensation; term plus one year; certificates and cancellation notice. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19 Warranties | Hosted Services warranted for the subscription term (§ 19.2), but perpetually/paid-up licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for 90 days. Amended § 19.2 to 12 months for Deliverables consisting of or embedding such software; 90 days retained for other Deliverables. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following are at our stated walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity / sole-supplier commitment.** An open-ended, term-length restriction on where we source hosted analytics, with no category limit, time limit or performance-based exit. It is internally inconsistent with § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment). We require deletion; the fallback we can offer is a named competing product, term only, capped at 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day, uncapped, triggered by delay in an undefined "dependency". Exposure could exceed the remaining contract value. Our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; if Vendor needs a fixed sum, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** An unqualified obligation to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier. Deletion is required; MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access.** Direct or remote access to our systems is not available, and § 22.2 already contradicts it. We accept the § 22.2 5% underpayment cost-allocation threshold as drafted.

---

## 4. Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline.** Deletions at §§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6 and 12.4; amendments at §§ 8.2, 19.2 and 22.1; new § 9.4 (Customer termination for convenience, 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund consistent with the existing § 10.2 refund mechanic).
2. **Frame the four walk-away items together** in the cover note so Vendor understands they are not trade-able against the compliant clauses at §§ 13, 14, 20, 21 and 24, which we are not reopening.
3. **Flag the internal inconsistencies** created by § 2.2 (against §§ 2.1 and 12.3) and § 22.1 (against § 22.2), and by § 12.4 (against § 12.3). Deleting the offending provisions resolves each conflict and should be an easy concession for Vendor's drafters. Deleting § 7.2 also resolves the duplicate "7.2" numbering with the invoicing clause.
4. **Confirm one factual point with Vendor** for the § 19.2 warranty: if all software is in fact delivered hosted, we can accept 90 days across the board and withdraw the 12-month amendment.
5. **Hold fallbacks in reserve** for the second round: 60-day non-renewal notice (§ 8.2); mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to involved personnel with standard carve-outs (§ 12.4); scope-limited, time-capped exclusivity (§ 2.2); capped early-termination fee in lieu of § 7.6.
6. **Route to the business** for confirmation that a 30-day convenience right and the removal of exclusivity align with the sourcing roadmap before we send."}
